messages:
Alice: Heads-up: I'm proposing a schema migration to decouple the console/analytics read model from the ingest envelope. Goal: smaller, query-friendly read table (metrics by window) + a read-adapter so the Console UI shape doesn't need a big refactor. Need a canary + backfill plan.

Ben: Quick Q — will this change break the console API or dashboards? Any signal we can use to flip back fast?

Alice: Short answer: no forced UX change. We plan dual-write from ingest to both route_metrics_v1 and route_metrics_v2, and add an adapter layer that can synthesize v1 rows from v2 until we cut over. Feature-flagged per-route rollback.

Cara: DDL sketch so folks can grok shape:
```sql
CREATE TABLE route_metrics_v2 (
  route_id uuid NOT NULL,
  window_start timestamptz NOT NULL,
  metrics jsonb NOT NULL, -- compacted counters/histograms
  route_profile_id uuid, -- optional FK for fast quotas join
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  PRIMARY KEY (route_id, window_start)
);
CREATE INDEX ON route_metrics_v2 USING gin (metrics jsonb_path_ops);
```

Cara: v2 keeps time-window as first-class key so range queries for dashboards are cheaper.

Diego: Important: quotas + routing policies rely on several denormalized fields in v1 (quota_bucket, tenant_id, policy_version). We need to either keep those in v2 or ensure the read adapter joins to route_metadata. I vote we include minimal denorm fields to avoid extra joins for hot queries.

Emily: Rollout UX: propose feature flag `use_route_metrics_v2` default=false. Canary to 5% tenants (random by tenant_id hash) + 2 internal tenants for stress tests. Add a fallback that rewrites queries to v1 if adapter latency > 50ms. Also add an admin toggle to force route-level fallback. :eyes:

Ben: Backfill: streaming job that reads v1 timeline and writes idempotent v2 rows. Two modes: historical bulk (spark job) and steady-state streaming for near-real-time. How long estimate for historic backfill for 6 months?

Alice: Estimate ~36-48h cluster job at current ingest volume for 6 months on our staging-sized cluster. We'll iterate. We'll ship dual-write first, then small incremental backfills to validate counts.

ingest-bot: deploy/streaming-ingest-job started: pipeline route-metrics-dualwrite-v1-v2 @staging

Ben: Query compatibility: adapter will expose the v1 projection to Console using a thin SQL view (or materialized view for some metrics). If we detect missing fields, adapter falls back to join with route_metadata. We should add automated tests that run dashboard queries against both systems and diff counts p50/p90/p99.

Cara: Practical checklist for rollout:
- dual-write implemented and smoke-tested in staging
- small canary (2 internal tenants) -> compare derived dashboards
- run streaming backfill for 30d window -> compare aggregates
- canary to 5% external tenants -> monitor latency/cost/accuracy
- increase to 100% + deprecate v1 or keep as archive

Diego: Monitoring: track per-route divergence metric (abs(delta)/baseline) and alert if >1% of routes have >5% divergence for 30m. Also track query latency and GIN index hit ratio.

Emily: UX/ops: add Console flag UI to flip per-tenant and a rollout page that shows divergence, backfill progress, and cost delta. Product wants a single click rollback.

Alice: One debate: do we compress metrics into a single jsonb (fewer columns) vs typed columns for frequent fields (p99, request_count). Tradeoff: jsonb reduces DDL churn and supports flexible rollout, typed columns better for indexes and pruning. I'm leaning jsonb + a few typed columns for the hottest signals.

Ben: Agree with hybrid. Put request_count, error_count, p95_latency as typed columns and everything else in metrics jsonb.

Cara: Will add acceptance test that runs old and new adapter for a period and asserts 99.9% equivalence on the typed columns.

Alice: Next actions: Cara & Ben implement DDL + adapter proof-of-concept, Diego & ingest team wire dual-write + backfill job, Emily designs feature flag + console rollout UI. We'll sync again Thurs 11am.

Diego: I'll also add a temporary read-adapter feature flag that disables adapter and lets console hit v1 directly for debugging.

Emily: love the plan. Add monitoring dashboards to `eng-platform` Grafana and a runbook for rollback steps. :+1:

Alice: Thanks everyone — I'll open the PRs and a runbook doc. If you want to be on the canary list ping me.
